newsitem.title: USA: NY-NJ Port Authority sets $100 mln bond sale in Q2.
newsitem.headline: NY-NJ Port Authority sets $100 mln bond sale in Q2.

text.p: The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey plans to sell about $100 million of consolidated bonds towards the end of the second quarter, its chief financial officer said on Wednesday.

Charles McClafferty also said, "We expect that at the end of the third quarter, the beginning of the fourth quarter, we'll be selling approximately another $300 million in bonds for new money and to refund our commercial paper obligations."
The chief financial officer made the remarks during an interview with Reuters Financial Television, parts of which were scheduled to be shown on Thursday.

Further, the Port Authority, which plans to break ground this autumn on a project to allow passengers to travel by rail to and from John F. Kennedy International Airport in Queens County, New York City, expects to sell bonds to help finance the $1.2 billion rail link after it gets going.
"It is likely that we will be issuing some sort of bonds backed by passenger facility charges in 1998 or 1999 because we'll be spending the money faster than we can collect it," McClafferty said.

He said the Port Authority wanted to use pay-as-you-go financing as much as possible, and the $3 charge per passenger, which will generate from $60 million to $70 million a year from New York City's two airports, will not provide enough money quickly enough.
The Port Authority has yet to decide how much new debt it might need to sell for the rail link. "It's really too premature to tell. It depends upon the timing and project payments," McClafferty said.
Rail-link proposals submitted by a handful of companies are now being reviewed.
The Port Authority official was confident the system would go ahead. "I see no reason why that project won't go forward successfully," McClafferty said.

Asked about concerns that the Kennedy airport rail link might be stalled by other proposals, like one for a rail link for LaGuardia Airport, McClafferty replied: "I'm not saying every political obstacle has been cleared out of the way."
While the Port Authority at present has no plans for a rail link for LaGuardia, it is working on a high-speed ferry system for that airport.
